podcast.title: Accidental Bass Distortion on "Rocket 88"
podcast.body: During the recording session for "Rocket 88" on March 2nd, 1951, bass player Willie Kizart's amplifier was accidentally dropped, jarring loose the speaker cone. This resulted in a distinctive buzz and vibration. Producer Sam Phillips decided to embrace this "cool" distorted sound, which became a new and defining characteristic of the track, potentially making it the first rock and roll record. "But then producer Sam Phillips, a white guy, said, hold on, sounds kind of cool. Let's use it as is."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Buzz-Inducing Guitar Amp Recording
podcast.body: In early March 1951, while heading to Memphis to record, the band had a flat tire. During the unloading of their car to access the spare, a guitar amplifier fell and dislodged its speaker cone. Lacking funds for a new amp or repairs, they improvised by stuffing newspaper around the cone, which created a distinctive "buzz" that became a defining characteristic of their song "Rocket 88." "On the way, they had a flat tire, and as they were unloading the car to get at the spare, a guitar amp hit the ground, knocking the speaker cone loose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Claim to First Rock and Roll Record
podcast.body: While the exact "first rock and roll record" is debated, "Rocket 88" by Jackie Brenston and his Delta Cats is strongly nominated, largely because producer Sam Phillips consistently touted it as such. Phillips' endorsement, coming from the discoverer of Elvis Presley, helped solidify this legend into a widely accepted fact. "It was because Sam Phillips said it was."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recording Journey to Sun Studios
podcast.body: On March 2nd, 1951, the Delta Cats packed into a station wagon with their instruments and drove 75 miles from Clarksdale, Mississippi, where they had been rehearsing at the Riverside Hotel, to Sun Studios in Memphis along Highway 61 to record. "On March 2nd 1951, all the Delta Cats packed up an old station wagon in front of the Riverside Hotel in Clarkstale, Mississippi where they'd been rehearsing and were ready to make a record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
